clinicalSignificance.comment: TEMPLATE, NOT READY TO SUBMIT. Heterozygous frameshift in POLE exon 2 (stop at codon 53 of 2,286). The variant is already in ClinVar (VCV000548779) with conflicting classifications: Pathogenic for recessive POLE deficiency reasoning (Labcorp Genetics/Invitae) and Uncertain significance (Ambry Genetics; Counsyl). For the condition named below (CRCS12, a dominant disorder caused by exonuclease-domain missense variants) loss-of-function variants are not an established mechanism (Mur et al. 2020, PMID 32792570). Phenotype of the one individual observed here: about 20 gastric and colonic polyps removed since age 19 (histology reports being collected; most advanced reported finding high-grade dysplasia), stage I papillary thyroid carcinoma, and other findings listed below. No tumour has been sequenced, so tumour mutational burden and mutational signatures are unknown. A 47-gene hereditary cancer panel was otherwise negative. The classification entered here is the submitter's decision; 'Uncertain significance' is a placeholder that matches the evidence for this condition.

attribute.value: Female patient with about 20 gastric and colonic polyps removed since age 19 (histology reports being collected; most advanced reported finding high-grade dysplasia), Stage I papillary thyroid carcinoma (1.2 cm, isthmus, encapsulated, non-invasive, cystic variant with extensive squamous metaplasia; age ~28; s/p total thyroidectomy), Stage IV+ deep infiltrating endometriosis with trans-diaphragmatic extension and pelvic free fluid, diffuse adenomyosis requiring ovarian-sparing total hysterectomy, bilateral proliferative breast changes with IHC-confirmed PASH (CD34+, CK AE1/AE3-), liver hypervascular lesion (hemangioma vs FNH, segment VII, 16x14 mm), congenital duplicated inferior vena cava, and ANA 1:160 with AC-21 pattern. Family history: maternal grandmother with uterine cancer and ductal breast cancer. Comorbidities: hEDS, POTS, gastroparesis. Negative for FILS syndrome, intellectual disability, and neurodevelopmental conditions.
